exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included women with triplet pregnancies from 26 weeks' gestation onward at a tertiary center between 2000 and 2020.
finding: Women attempting vaginal delivery in triplet pregnancies achieved a 90% success rate, with VD associated with lower risks for neonatal sepsis and retinopathy of prematurity compared to CD, though unadjusted risks for IRDS and IVH were higher.
mod_finding: Compared to cesarean delivery, vaginal delivery in triplet pregnancies was associated with lower risks of neonatal sepsis and retinopathy of prematurity, but unadjusted risks for infant respiratory distress syndrome and interventricular hemorrhage were higher, becoming non-significant after gestational age adjustment.
